verdict.rationale: Paperspace documents Notebooks as a web-based Jupyter IDE and says users can connect to remote Jupyter kernels through alternative IDEs. Machines also support SSH access. However, the docs never name VS Code or Cursor or describe a one-step launch or connect flow, and one hands-on user reports that getting SSH access to Core VMs was 'an uphill battle.' Missing for 10: documented one-click Jupyter launch on Machines, named VS Code/Cursor remote-connect integration, evidence the flow is single-step, independent corroboration of a smooth IDE connection.

support.subject: As a developer, I can open Jupyter or connect my IDE (VS Code/Cursor) to the instance in one step

citations.quote: Notebooks are a web-based Jupyter IDE with shared persistent storage for long-term development and inter-notebook collaboration, backed by accelerated compute.
Connect to remote Jupyter kernels through alternative IDEs.
You can connect to your Linux or Windows-based machine using the Paperspace console or desktop app using SSH connection.
